newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine shares shuffle over peso fears.
newsitem.headline: Philippine shares shuffle over peso fears.

text.p: Fears over how far the peso would fall took the fire out of Philippine shares on Monday and analysts said the market would shuffle aimlessly until the currency settled.

After a flying start, the main index started to lose steam at mid-session and plodded to the finish, closing 9.59 points up at 2,710.73, as investors waited for signs of stability in the currency market.

"A lot of people are still quite unsure as to where our peso is headed," said Ramon Saulo, senior investment analyst of Asiamerit Securities. "When that uncertainy dies down that's when things will come back to normal."
Losers edged gainers 66 to 53, with the large number of unchanged issues, 61, showing investors were still hedging their bets, analysts said. Turnover was 3.1 billion pesos.
The market posted its biggest single-day rise in percentage terms in nearly seven years on Friday after the central bank effectively devalued the peso by letting it float in a wider band.
Firms expected to benefit the most from a depreciated peso, such as phone company PLDT, power firm Meralco's B shares and electronics firm Ionics, rose again on Monday.
But profit-taking cooled other issues that helped push the market to its 7.57 percent rise on Friday, traders said.
The market showed its insecurity at mid-session when it slipped into negative territory, falling to a low of 2,695.33, before regaining its bearings.
"... we will be seeing more of a roller-coaster ride this week or even up to next week," said chief technical analyst Jonathan Ravelas of Asian Capital Equities.
He added the fairly large number of unchanged issues was a sign that that investors were staying on the sidelines.
"People would want the story (of the exchange rate) to settle down before taking their positions," Ravelas added.
Traders said investors realised it would take at least a week before the central bank lowered its overnight interest rates, which it raised last week to 32 percent in an attempt to defend the peso.
"The central bank is holding on to its shield," said one trader.
With the debate on whether the peso would be depreciated now behind it, the market might finally be over the hump, said Saturnino Mejia, research head at Guoco Securities.
"The likely gainers are those issues which are positively affected by the devaluation, companies whose earnings are primarily foreign currency based," Mejia said.
Besides PLDT and Meralco, an attractive buy would be Jollibee Foods, a fast-food chain with a growing number of franchises abroad, Mejia said.
One of the day's biggest winners was Meralco B whose shares sugged more than nine percent, or 13 pesos, closing at 155 pesos.
Analysts said a factor boosting the stock was the likelihood of power rate increases after the peso depreciation.
Energy Secretary Francisco Viray said he expected domestic power rates to rise.
"We don't know how much it will be at this point," he said, adding they also depended on the price of imported crude.
